clue.text: Anthropophagic, it's a wild and wicked beast

indicators.note: wild letters run free, so these clue words are rearranged

parts.note: anthropophagic means man-eating, the source of the word man, which in the answer is swallowed by the other shuffled letters
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A warning about a savage creature that eats people.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, 'Anthropophagic' (man-eating) has the shuffled IT'S A ('wild') eat MAN, giving TAS-MAN-I; treated here as one pool, as the result is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial, an animal found on the Australian island state.

clue.text: German river leading, in essence, to Cologne, do we hear?

indicators.note: the question asks whether we hear the words, so it is their sound that counts

parts.note: in the scent eau de Cologne, the words that come before Cologne are eau de

explanation.surface: A query about a river flowing toward the city of Cologne, perhaps in essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eau de' (French for 'water of') is said much like the river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Order of Mammalia yielding religious figure (not lama)

indicators.note: an order of letters is a rearrangement, and here the clue's mammal word is put in a new order once the other word's letters are set aside

explanation.surface: A zoological classification of mammals producing a holy man, though not a Tibetan lama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not lama' tells you the letters of LAMA leave MAMMALIA; 'Order of' rearranges the remaining MMIA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Exchange online giants Massenet, Brahms & Liszt?

indicators.note: Brahms and Liszt is rhyming slang for pissed, i.e. drunk, so the composer names below are scrambled

explanation.surface: Composers as giants of music, pictured trading notes on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms & Liszt' is British rhyming slang for drunk ('pissed'), so GIANTS MASSENET is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant messaging is real-time text chat over the internet, a conversational exchange done online.

clue.text: Perhaps Idomeneo and Flavio hope to undress before Overture to Swan Lake

indicators.note: undressing strips the outer layer, so the clue word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: an overture comes at the start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Opera lovers hoping to strip off before the start of Tchaikovsky's ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that the two operas are examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo (Mozart) and Flavio (Handel) are examples of serious Italian opera, plural of opera seria.

clue.text: Express delivery part of its service?

definitions.text: Express delivery part of its service?

parts.words: Express delivery part of its service
parts.note: the Express is a British daily newspaper, and its delivery to doorsteps is done on a round by a newsagent's boy or girl

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a fast courier or postal option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like 'fast' but is the Daily Express newspaper; the British teenage job of delivering papers fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper round is a regular route delivering newspapers, so it delivers each day's Express to subscribers.

clue.text: A lax body — most common in mums — during surgery, finally tucked up?

indicators.note: during means within, so the following letters are set within the shuffled ones
lax means loose, so the letters of the clue word are loosened into a new order

parts.note: the letter M occurs twice in mums, more than any other
in op is a common phrase for being in surgery; op is short for operation
finally means at last

explanation.surface: A slack midriff, so common in mothers, being dealt with in an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lax' shuffles the body; 'most common in mums' is the letter appearing most often there, and 'during' does double duty as the IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominoplasty is the surgical name for a tummy tuck, removing loose skin from the stomach.

clue.text: 'Our Father Time/Who art a weather vane/Hallowed be thy ground …'?

definitions.text: 'Our Father Time/Who art a weather vane/Hallowed be thy ground …'?

parts.words: 'Our Father Time/Who art a weather vane/Hallowed be thy ground …'?
parts.note: a parody of the opening of the Christian prayer, recast for Lord's cricket ground, whose famous weather vane shows Father Time

explanation.surface: A cricket lover's comic version of a church prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground; its Father Time weather vane makes the parody a prayer to Lord's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer begins 'Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name', which these lines parody.

clue.text: The writer's prudish, having exposed adult book licence

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, so the writer's is I'm
prim means prudish

indicators.note: exposing strips off the covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: mature means adult

explanation.surface: A writer who is too prim to have an explicit adult book licensed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having exposed' takes the outside letters off MATURE, leaving ATUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprimatur is an official licence to print, historically granted by the Church to a book.

clue.text: Between five and fifty, this palm would be essential

indicators.note: the answer is what lies between the two numbers, so their letters are stripped from the outside of the longer word

parts.note: vital means essential
V is the Roman numeral for five
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a number range where a palm tree is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' stands for the answer: placed between V and L (Roman 5 and 50) it would make VITAL, meaning essential.
explanation.definitionFit: The ita is a South American palm tree, the miriti or moriche palm.

clue.text: See fencing exercise scratching face? It shouldn't

definitions.text: See fencing exercise scratching face? It shouldn't

indicators.note: fencing encloses, so the clue word's remaining letters wrap round the exercise
scratching off the face means removing the first letter

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school exercise lesson

explanation.surface: Watch a fencing drill where a face is scratched, which ought not to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: A fencing sword should never scratch an opponent's face, so the whole clue also describes the weapon; 'fencing' is the container signal and 'scratching face' the beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: The épée is one of the three fencing weapons, a heavy blade with a button tip.

clue.text: Monster really will sacrifice wings to be human

indicators.note: losing its wings, each word sheds its outer parts, leaving letters from the middle of the two words

explanation.surface: A beast that gives up its wings to become a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed the outer letters around the join of 'Monster really' to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's line 'To err is human' makes making mistakes the defining human trait.

clue.text: Some relief from the rants of Mad John Bull?

parts.note: John Bull is the personification of England, so ENG, an abbreviation for English
ravings are the wild rants of someone mad

explanation.surface: Seeking relief from an angry Englishman's tirades.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bull is the stock cartoon figure of a stout Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is cut into a surface, and relief printing and carving produce such prints.

clue.text: Crude hire covers University of Little Enlightenment

indicators.note: covers means goes over and around, so the hire word wraps the other letters

parts.note: rental means hire
dim means not bright, of little enlightenment

explanation.surface: A rough hire deal involving a university that teaches very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimental means basic or undeveloped, so primitive and rough, like something crude.

clue.text: Volume: a pretty tiny novel within a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the word before it are made new by rearrangement

parts.note: fair means pretty

explanation.surface: A book volume described as a small, pretty novel inside another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' signals the shuffle of tiny. Vanity Fair is also the fair inside Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, hence 'within a novel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray wrote this famous Victorian book about Becky Sharp.

clue.text: You'll see this man, initially cornered in board meeting, rip off flier

definitions.text: You'll see this man, initially cornered in board meeting
definitions.meaning: a chess piece, which starts the game in the corner of the board
a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A man trapped in a board meeting tears off a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' is a chess game, not a company gathering; 'flier' is a bird, not a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle, swindle and crow are all covered by this one word, a triple definition.

clue.text: Reason for securing airfields?

indicators.note: the reason is given for the securing, so securing comes first in the answer

parts.note: landing a fish or a deal is securing it
grounds are a reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Asking why someone is taking control of airports.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing grounds are places where aircraft can touch down, rough airstrips or airfields.

clue.text: See 17
See 4
Returning student doctor not entirely the same

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the trimmed word is read backwards
not entirely means its last letter is left off

parts.note: a medic is a medical student or doctor

explanation.surface: A trainee doctor coming back, not quite the same as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MEDIC to MEDI, and 'Returning' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for 'the same', used in references to repeat the previous source.

clue.text: Advice about border wind up southern range

indicators.note: about means around, so the advice word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
a hem is a border on cloth
to wind up is to end

explanation.surface: Guidance about winding up a southern frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendip Hills form a range of hills, so the plural name stands for that range.

clue.text: With regular saves on field, no goals

indicators.note: regular saves means keeping every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper making regular saves on the pitch, so the score stays blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is the score of zero, as when a team scores nothing in a match.

clue.text: City Bank failing to appoint head of RBC

indicators.note: failing to appoint someone means they are left out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: the head is the first letter

explanation.surface: A city bank that has not appointed a chief for the Royal Bank of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.

clue.text: Scandinavian heptad, now deserted by leader of eight

indicators.note: being deserted by someone means they leave, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a heptad is a group of seven

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: A group of seven Scandinavians now abandoned by the head of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sven is a common Swedish man's name, so a Scandinavian person.

clue.text: Quirk of taxing Formula One scrap, keeping heat right up

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: F1 written with the digit read as I
a rag is a scrap of cloth
to scald is to heat almost to boiling

explanation.surface: A tax quirk tied to motor racing, with a heated fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One is written F1, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal drag pulls taxpayers into higher bands when thresholds don't rise with inflation, a quirk of the tax system.

clue.text: Some uttered an expression of relief

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: phew is an expression of relief, so an expression of relief is a phew

explanation.surface: Several people voiced their relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A few means a small number, so some in the sense of several.

clue.text: No alfresco party to ruin!

parts.note: a do is a party
not alfresco, i.e. not outdoors, is in

explanation.surface: An indoor party being spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in is to destroy or kill, so to ruin something completely.

clue.text: Naked logic exploited failing — Kirk didn't see adversaries using it

definitions.text: Kirk didn't see adversaries using it

indicators.note: exploited means worked or used, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a vice is a failing or weakness

explanation.surface: Naked logic being used to point out a flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: In Star Trek, Captain Kirk's Klingon and Romulan enemies hid their ships from view with this technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloaking device makes a starship invisible, so a captain cannot see an enemy ship.
